title: Packing Instrumental and Locative Details into Participial Modifiers

sections.title: Material and Means with -val/-vel Inside the Participial Phrase
sections.content: In architectural and art-historical descriptions, Hungarian regularly embeds instrumental complements (-val/-vel, 'with/in') inside pre-nominal participial clauses to specify materials, glazes, or techniques: a színes mázzal bevont kerámiák ('the ceramics coated with colorful glaze') or a fémes fényben játszó eozinmáz ('the eosin glaze playing in metallic light').

sections.title: Locative and Manner Modifiers Before the Participle
sections.content: Locative phrases (a Zsolnay-gyárban kifejlesztett) and manner phrases (magas hőfokon kiégetett) can stack sequentially before the noun without needing a single relative pronoun: a Zsolnay-gyárban kifejlesztett, magas hőfokon kiégetett pirogránit.

sections.title: Multi-Complement Pre-Nominal Participial Modifiers
rows: the roof tiles coated with colorful glaze
the pyrogranite fired at a high temperature
the Zsolnay roofs sparkling in the sunshine
the eosin glaze named after the flush of dawn

items.spanish: A Zsolnay-gyárban kifejlesztett pirogránit teljesen fagyállónak bizonyult.
items.english: The pyrogranite developed in the Zsolnay factory proved completely frost-resistant.

items.spanish: A színes mázzal bevont kerámiák a falusi fazekasság formáit emelték át a nagyvárosba.
items.english: The ceramics coated with colorful glaze transferred the forms of village pottery into the metropolis.

sections.title: B2 Usage Notice
sections.content: When stacking two participial modifiers before a single noun, separate them with a comma: a magas hőfokon kiégetett, színes mázzal bevont kerámiák.
